title: An option is fair when implied volatility equals realized volatility
summary: The speaker defines fair value as implied volatility equal to realized volatility. Implied usually trades a bit above realized, so options usually carry a small premium. The further IV sits above RV, the richer the option. Many wheel traders sell IV blindly and may sell fairly priced options; for an edge, look for high IV on an absolute level and high IV relative to RV.

params.label: IV premium over RV
params.help: Average points that implied vol trades above realized vol.

steps.caption: A stock path with its realized and implied volatility.
Realized volatility: how much the stock actually moves. This is the fair level for implied vol.
Implied volatility usually sits a little above realized: a small premium over fair value.
The wider IV is above RV, the richer the option. Sell rich options and buy cheap ones.
Selling blindly, without this check, can mean selling options at fair value with no edge.

takeaways: An option is fairly priced when implied volatility equals realized volatility.
Implied usually trades above realized, so options are usually a little rich.
For an edge, sell options with high IV and a wide gap over RV, not IV alone.
caveats: The speaker's VAY screener is promotional and not verified here.
Defining fair value as IV equal to RV is the speaker's view; it ignores jump and event risk.
